newsitem.title: CHINA: Construction under way on $24 mln south China wharf.
newsitem.headline: Construction under way on $24 mln south China wharf.

text.p: Construction has begun on a $24 million wharf in southeast China aimed at speeding development of silica sand resources in the area, the Xinhua news agency said on Saturday.
It said the 25,000-tonne multi-purpose Chengan wharf was being built in Dongshan county in Fujian province.
Some of the funding on the project is from Hong Kong. There were no details of which Hong Kong company had a role in the project or how big a stake it had.
Dongshan now has two 5,000-tonne wharves and one 3,000-tonne petroleum wharf.
The new wharf is scheduled to have an annual 1.1 million-tonne handling capacity in two years.
